idiom_name: System.Text.Json JsonConverter<T>/JsonConverterFactory registry bound to canonical types
implementation_notes: System.Text.Json supplies both mechanical steps: a JsonConverter<T> (or a JsonConverterFactory, registered once in JsonSerializerOptions.Converters) reads one source layout through Utf8JsonReader and replaces the hand-written per-format translator, while [JsonPolymorphic]/[JsonDerivedType] (or a converter's explicit switch on the discriminator) replaces the router by binding each wire tag to a concrete canonical type. What the framework does NOT do is the mapping: converting a partner's field names, units, currencies and dates into the canonical record stays hand-written inside Read/Write. Hand-rolled dispatching remains justified when the sources are not JSON at all (CSV, fixed-width, binary), when detection has to be heuristic (root element, file name), or when one converter must accept several discriminator spellings.
pitfalls: Converters are selected by declared type, so every source layout that must produce the same canonical type needs its own input shape (or converter); collapsing them into one class is where misrouting starts.

Match the reader options to the contract (AllowTrailingCommas, PropertyNameCaseInsensitive, NumberHandling): a converter that silently accepts case-different names hides producer drift instead of reporting it.
A canonical type without a parameterless constructor or [JsonConstructor] fails only at run time and only for some source layouts, so cover each layout with a deserialization test.

variants.name: [JsonPolymorphic]/[JsonDerivedType] attribute binding on the canonical base type
variants.implementation_notes: Declarative variant: mark the canonical base type with [JsonPolymorphic(TypeDiscriminatorPropertyName = "type")] and each source shape with [JsonDerivedType(typeof(...), "csv")] so the serializer reads and writes the discriminator itself and instantiates the matching type - the router and the per-format translator collapse into attributes plus one Read method per derived record. Choose it when the wire tag is stable and trustworthy, and keep an explicit converter when discriminator values must be remapped, several wire tags map to one type, or the source is not JSON.
variants.code_sketch:
[JsonPolymorphic(TypeDiscriminatorPropertyName = "type")]
[JsonDerivedType(typeof(CsvOrder), "csv")]
[JsonDerivedType(typeof(XmlOrder), "xml")]
public abstract record Order { public required string Id { get; init; } }
public sealed record CsvOrder(string Raw) : Order;

var wire = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Order>(payload);   // library picks the subtype by tag
var canonical = OrderMapper.ToCanonical(wire);           // one shape reaches consumers
pitfalls: An unknown discriminator value fails by default (or falls back to the base type if configured), so set UnknownDerivedTypeHandling deliberately and route the failure to the invalid-message channel.
Attributes are compiled in: a new partner format still needs a code change and a redeploy, so the declarative route is not a configuration-only route.
Exposing the derived wire records as the domain model leaks wire discriminators into business code; map to the canonical record immediately.
